translation.english_title: Why does the love-dove speak into the ear?

english_lines: Why does the love-dove speak into the ear? —
Was the affection I bore all in vain?...
Why was I born a maiden?...
notes: The love-dove and secret-in-the-ear images remain literal and intimate rather than being rewritten as `love whispers to me`.
The repeated `பாவை ஏன் பிறந்தேனோ?` is retained as a direct existential lament.

english_lines: The young queen with a tender-shoot body has withered,
To end this sorrow... you... come...
notes: `தளிர்மேனி` remains the tender-shoot body image instead of becoming merely `delicate` or `young`.
The repeated `வா` and broken ellipses remain audible in English.

english_lines: In a forest where a deer-skinned tiger lives,
Was the affection I bore all in vain?...
Why was I born a maiden?...
notes: The verified source deliberately preserves the spaced phrase `மான் தோல்`; the English keeps the unsettling `deer-skinned tiger` image instead of silently repairing or explaining it away.
`மாங்குயில்` remains `mango-cuckoo`, preserving the source's compound image rather than reducing it to `bird`.

english_lines: The queen has fallen into darkness where sorrow dwells,
notes: The sorrow/darkness and sleeping moon-maiden images remain concrete; the English does not generalize them into `bring me hope`.

english_lines: Through love itself I was deceived,
Will none of my dreams of desire come true?
Was the affection I bore all in vain?
Why was I born a maiden?...
notes: The source's love/deception reversal remains direct; it is not softened into disappointment.
The final refrain returns almost unchanged, preserving the song's circular lament.
The abbreviated source cue remains a cue; absent refrain text is not reconstructed.

translator_notes: The translation preserves the source's recurring love-dove, maiden, tender-shoot body, breeze, deer-skinned tiger, mango-cuckoo, darkness and moon-maiden images rather than smoothing them into generic heartbreak.
The source role label `பூங்காவனம்` remains exact and no singer is inferred.
This is a literary source-faithful translation, not a singable adaptation.
